newsitem.title: JAPAN: TIFFE euroyen off highs as stocks pare losses.
newsitem.headline: TIFFE euroyen off highs as stocks pare losses.

text.p: The key March three-month euroyen futures contract was off earlier highs in late Tuesday trade after the stock market pared earlier losses and Japanese bond yields came off lows, dealers said.

Traders said sentiment stayed bullish and activity was mainly led by stock and bond market movements, but a lack of fresh evidence of a worsening Japanese economy prompted traders to take profits before a 99.20 yen resistance.
A trust bank dealer said the market would closely watch the release of Japan's machinery orders data for June and forecasts for the July-to-September quarter due out on Friday.
Key three-month certificates of deposit (CDs) were issued at 0.62 percent in volume of 50 billion yen, while 200 billion yen of two-month CDs were issued at 0.63 percent.

The key overnight call rate was mainly traded at 0.50 percent. In the morning, the Bank of Japan drained a net 500 billion yen from the money market, against a projected fund surplus of 680 billion yen. The market had been expecting a drainage of 400 billion yen.
